intro: An old-time fiddler from the Bronx.
story: Bruce Molsky was born in 1955 in the Bronx and found old-time music while studying engineering at Cornell. He moved south in 1976 to learn from the Mount Airy fiddler Tommy Jarrell and became a full-time musician after turning 40. He played Pickathon in 2011 and 2012, and shared a Grammy nomination for Fiddlers 4 with Michael Doucet, Darol Anger and Rushad Eggleston. He played banjo, fiddle and guitar on Mark Knopfler's 2015 album Tracker, and Closing the Gap, with his Mountain Drifters, came in 2019.
artist_reel_line: Closing the Gap, with his Mountain Drifters, came out in 2019; he keeps teaching and touring.

story: Doug Paisley spent a decade in bluegrass bands before his 2008 solo debut on the Brooklyn label No Quarter. Constant Companion, released October 12, 2010 with cameos from Feist and Garth Hudson, drew praise from Rolling Stone, Mojo and the New Yorker and made the 2011 Polaris Prize long list. He played Pickathon in 2012, the year of the Golden Embers EP. Strong Feelings came in January 2014, Starter Home in 2018 and Sad Old World in 2024.
artist_reel_line: Sad Old World, in 2024, kept his unhurried pace.

story: Typhoon is a Portland collective led by the singer-songwriter Kyle Morton, known for a big horn and string lineup. Hunger and Thirst, on Tender Loving Empire in 2010, drew year-end praise, including a spot among Willamette Week's favorites. They played Pickathon in 2010 and again in 2012. White Lighter came on Roll Call in 2013, Offerings in January 2018 and Sympathetic Magic in 2020. In January 2026 the band played two shows to mark twenty years, and in September a pastoral outdoor set on Sauvie Island.
artist_reel_line: In September 2026 they played a pastoral outdoor set on Sauvie Island.

story: White Denim formed in Austin in 2006 around James Petralli and Steve Terebecki, and Austin Jenkins joined as second guitarist in 2010. Fits brought a US deal with Downtown Records in 2009, D followed in 2011, and in 2012 they toured with Wilco and played Pickathon. Corsicana Lemonade, October 29, 2013, was partly produced by Wilco's Jeff Tweedy and was their first album on both the US and UK charts. The drummer Josh Block and Jenkins left in 2015 to join Leon Bridges, and the rebuilt band's Stiff reached the UK Top 20 in 2016. They followed 12, in 2024, with another studio record in 2026, still around Petralli.
artist_reel_line: They followed 12, in 2024, with another studio record in 2026.

story: Dr. Dog formed around 1999 in Philadelphia as an offshoot of an earlier project of Toby Leaman and Scott McMicken called Raccoon. Shame, Shame, on Anti- on April 6, 2010, was made with an outside producer; Be the Void, on February 7, 2012, was recorded in the band's own Philadelphia studio in about two months, and Relix heard the first studio record to approach their live energy. They had played Pickathon in 2009 and 2010 and returned in 2012. They went on to run their own studio and in-house label, releasing Critical Equation in 2018. After stepping back from full-time touring in 2021, they came back with the self-titled Dr. Dog on July 19, 2024.
artist_reel_line: Dr. Dog, the self-titled comeback, came out in July 2024.

story: The Hot 8 Brass Band was founded in New Orleans in 1995 by the tuba player Bennie Pete with Jerome Jones and Harry Cook, and became known for brass band takes on funk, hip hop and bounce. Rock With the Hot 8 came out on Tru Thoughts in October 2007, and its Sexual Healing single sold its first 500 copies at once, the fastest seller in the label's history. They played Pickathon in 2012. The Life & Times of the Hot 8 Brass Band came out that fall and was nominated for the 2014 Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album. They marked twenty years with Vicennial in 2015.
artist_reel_line: The Life & Times of the Hot 8 Brass Band drew a 2014 Grammy nomination.

intro: A Portland folk songwriter from Coquille, Oregon.
story: Laura Gibson was born in Coquille, Oregon, in 1979 and trained as a cellist before moving to Portland after college, where she became part of the Hush Records folk scene. Beasts of Seasons, in 2009, got an NPR First Listen billed as a quiet masterpiece. La Grande, her third solo album, came out on Barsuk in early 2012, and she says she decided on a trip to La Grande that it would err on the side of confidence and drop inhibitions; the BBC called it a gem both sleepy and steely. She played Pickathon in 2008, 2009 and 2012. Empire Builder followed in 2016, and in late 2026 she signed with Loose Music and released the single Sylvia.
artist_reel_line: In late 2026 she signed with Loose Music and released Sylvia.
